questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Autumn leaves __shuffled beneath him__ as he wandered through the quiet forest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **rustled underfoot**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"shuffled"** means to move with a dragging or scraping motion, often producing a soft sound. (घिसटना)

 
 
• **Example: **He shuffled his feet nervously while waiting for his turn to speak.
 
 
 
• **"Rustled"** refers to producing a soft, muffled sound, typically caused by the movement of dry leaves or paper. (सरसराना)
 
 
• **Example: **The wind rustled through the leaves, creating a soothing sound.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "rustled underfoot" is the most appropriate substitute for "shuffled beneath him," as it accurately describes the gentle sound made when walking on dry autumn leaves.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **rustled underfoot**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Crushed around** (चारों ओर कुचला): This implies something being pressed or flattened, which does not convey the sound of dry leaves being walked upon.

 
 
• **Example: **The crowd crushed around the stage to get a closer look at the performer.
 
 
 
• **Moved to another place** (दूसरी जगह स्थानांतरित): This refers to changing the position or location of something, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
 
• **Example: **The furniture was moved to another place to make room for the new carpet.
 
 
 
• **Died over** (मर गया): This phrase does not have any relevance in the context of the sentence, as it implies the end of life or cessation of something.
 
 
• **Example: **He died over a long illness that lasted several years.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

His artwork is / more intricate / than any artist / in the gallery.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. than any artist .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment "**than any artist**" is grammatically incorrect because the sentence compares the artwork to artists, which is illogical.
 
• The comparison should be between similar entities. The correct comparison should be "**than that of any artist**," referring to the artwork of the other artists.
 
• In English grammar, when comparing something belonging to a person or group, the possessive form or "that of" should be used to make the comparison clear and logical.

Correct sentence: *His artwork is more intricate than that of any artist in the gallery*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparison Rules:**
 
 
• When comparing two things, ensure that the entities being compared are of the same type (e.g., object to object, person to person).
 
• If the sentence involves possession, use "that of" or "those of" to clarify the comparison.
 
• Example: Her performance was better than **that of** her classmates.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Incorrect: This car is faster than any other driver.
 
• Correct: This car is faster than any other car.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:

• **Example: **The manager tried to appease the angry customers by offering them a discount.
 
 
 
• **"Pacify"** is the correct synonym for "Appease," as it also means to calm, soothe, or bring peace to a situation or a person. (शांत करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The mother pacified the crying baby by singing a lullaby.
 
 
 
• Hence, **"Pacify"** is the most appropriate synonym for "Appease."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Pacify**.

• **Appeal** (निवेदन): To make a serious or formal request for help, support, or a decision.
 
 
• **Example:** The charity made an appeal to the public for donations.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They worked / very hardly / on their project / for several weeks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. very hardly .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **“hardly”** is incorrect in this context. **"Hardly"** means "barely" or "almost not," which does not fit the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• The correct word to use here is **"hard."** The phrase should be *"They worked very hard on their project."*
 
• The error lies in the misuse of the adverb **"hardly."**

Correct sentence: *They worked very hard on their project for several weeks*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Difference between "hard" and "hardly":**

 
 
• **Hard:** An adverb that means "with a lot of effort." Example: She worked hard to complete the assignment.
 
• **Hardly:** An adverb that means "barely" or "almost not." Example: He hardly slept last night.
 
 
 
• Using **"very hardly"** is grammatically incorrect because **"hardly"** already expresses a limiting degree, and "very" cannot modify it in this context.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Poverty is the __urgent__ concern in India today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. most urgent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"urgent"** is an adjective that describes something requiring immediate attention.
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase **"Poverty is the urgent concern"** implies that poverty is the most pressing issue in India today.
 
• To correct the sentence grammatically and provide the intended emphasis, we use the superlative form of the adjective **"urgent"**, which is **"most urgent"**.

Correct sentence: *Poverty is the most urgent__ concern in India today.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective Forms:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Describes a quality without comparison.

 **Example:** This issue is urgent.
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Compares two things.

 **Example:** This issue is more urgent than others.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Describes the highest degree of a quality among three or more things.

 **Example:** Poverty is the most urgent concern.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Manoj has a bigger / farmhouse of one hundred / hectares near the city.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. "Manoj has a bigger".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains an error in the phrase "**Manoj has a bigger**."
 
• The use of the word "**bigger**" is incorrect in this context because the comparison is not clear or complete.
 
• In English, when using comparatives like "**bigger**," it is necessary to specify what is being compared. For example, "**bigger than what?**"
 
• A correct revision would be "**Manoj has a large farmhouse of one hundred hectares near the city**" if no comparison is being made, or "**Manoj has a bigger farmhouse than his neighbor**" if a comparison is intended.

Correct sentence: *Manoj has a large farmhouse of one hundred hectares near the city.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparatives and Superlatives:**
 
 
• **Comparatives:** Used to compare two things. Structure: "**Adjective + -er**" or "**more + adjective**" (e.g., taller, more beautiful).
 
• **Superlatives:** Used to indicate the highest degree among three or more things. Structure: "**Adjective + -est**" or "**most + adjective**" (e.g., tallest, most beautiful).
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:** Always ensure that the comparison is clear and complete when using comparatives.
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word segment that can replace the underlined part in the sentence.

The two thieves divided the looted money __with themselves.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. between themselves .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"with themselves"** is incorrect because it does not convey the correct relationship between the thieves while dividing the money.
 
• The correct preposition to use when something is divided or shared between two people is **"between"**.
 
• **"Among themselves"** is incorrect because it is used when there are more than two people involved, but in this case, there are only two thieves.
 
• The phrases **"of themselves"** and **"off themselves"** are grammatically incorrect and do not fit the context of the sentence.

Correct sentence: *The two thieves divided the looted money **between themselves**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Between vs. Among:**

 
 
• **Between:** Used when referring to two people, groups, or things. Example: The agreement was signed between the two companies.
 
• **Among:** Used when referring to more than two people, groups, or things. Example: The property was divided among the three siblings.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The water near the coast was __shallower__ and clean.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. shallow .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence mentions a comparison between the water near the coast and its depth or cleanliness.
 
• In this context, the correct adjective form should match the degree of comparison implied.
 
• The word **"shallow"** is correct because no comparative or superlative degree is explicitly required, and it is paired with "clean," which is also in the basic form.
 
• Using "shallowest" or "the shallowest" would imply a superlative comparison, which is not relevant here.
 
• "More shallow" suggests a comparative degree, which is unnecessary in this sentence as no comparison is being made.

Correct sentence: *The water near the coast was **shallow** and clean.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective Forms:**
 
 
• **Basic Form: **Shallow
 
• **Comparative Form: **More shallow (used for comparing two entities)
 
• **Superlative Form: **Shallowest (used for comparing three or more entities)
 
 
 
• **Usage of Adjectives:**
 
 
• **Basic Form:** Used when describing a single entity without comparison.
 
• **Comparative Form:** Used when comparing two entities (e.g., "The water here is more shallow than there").
 
• **Superlative Form:** Used when comparing three or more entities (e.g., "This is the shallowest water in the region").

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Destroy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e., **Ruin**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Destroy"** means to put an end to the existence of something by damaging or attacking it beyond repair. (नष्ट करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The heavy rains destroyed the crops in the fields.
 
 
 
• **"Ruin"** refers to causing great and irreparable damage or harm to something. It is synonymous with "destroy." (बर्बाद करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The earthquake ruined several buildings in the city.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'Destroy' **is **'Ruin'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Delight **(आनंद): A feeling of great pleasure or happiness.

 
 
• **Example: **She was filled with delight when she received the good news.
 
 
 
• **Decline **(अस्वीकार या गिरावट): To become smaller, fewer, or less; decrease.
 
 
• **Example: **There has been a decline in the number of visitors to the museum.
 
 
 
• **Fabricate **(गढ़ना): To invent or concoct something, typically with deceitful intent.
 
 
• **Example: **He fabricated an excuse to avoid attending the meeting.
